src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_triage/findings/emitters.ts:43-447 enumerates the nine sensors, none of which reasons about reachability or reconciles an inventory of what should exist; the technique's precondition — a scanner asked to prove an absence — is not among this pipeline's questions.

src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_triage/findings/sweep.ts:102-228 reads locally registered projects through in-process IPC, and the HTTP bridge at src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/dev_tools_http.rs:1-11 is loopback-only against registered roots; contents are not metered, so there is no allocation decision for a budget to make.

The technique's stated precondition is a scanner pointed at arbitrary foreign codebases where the population-first order is unavailable; every target here is a project the operator registered and the scanner may read freely, so precision is buyable by calibration rather than by scoping.

src/features/plugins/dev-tools/sub_triage/findings/usePassportForProject.ts:1-46 consumes generated state, and an invariant audit plus a dry-run repair protocol exist in Rust (context_audit.rs:26-38, dev_tools_http.rs:40-42), but I did not read them closely enough to say whether the repair names its anti-remedy or whether a drift journal exists for the unreachable-generator case.

pairs.registryProposal: Wall 3 of the golden path — 'Location down to the line, plus the matched content itself, quoted' — over-fits to text-pattern sensors and has no formulation for the threshold-over-telemetry sensor this pipeline is built from. Six of its nine emitters (LLM cost pinpoints, Sentry issue rates, dormant skills, doc rot, disputed memories, KPI attention) produce findings of the form 'this measured number crossed its threshold', for which there is no line to quote; emitters.ts:11-13 states the honest alternative — carry the raw numbers the threshold decision was made on. That choice then makes verify.ts:4-6,14 possible ('a fresh emit IS the probe'), which re-measures the quantity rather than re-reading a location, and is arguably a stronger verifier than the golden path's re-grep because it distinguishes moved from unchanged (verify.ts:134-145) rather than merely present from absent. Proposal: split wall 3's evidence requirement by sensor class — quoted-and-located for pattern sensors, measured-value-plus-threshold for aggregate sensors — and let finding-lifecycle's verification pass name the re-measure as a legitimate second form.

pairs.subject: webhook-ingestion
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/tools/triggers.rs:1742 replays `log_entry.body`, which src-tauri/src/engine/webhook.rs:304 already replaced with the literal string '[redacted: see encrypted persona_event payload]', so every replay delivers that placeholder instead of the bytes that exposed the bug.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/smee_relay.rs:418 makes verification opt-in and absent by default ('when unset (the default) we cannot authenticate inbound events and accept them as before', :41-43), which is the accept-everything fallback the technique bans, on the mouth the file itself calls the highest-volume attacker-reachable producer (:727-739); src-tauri/src/engine/cloud_webhook_relay.rs has no sender verification at all. The direct listener is exemplary by contrast — raw bytes verified before parse (webhook.rs:287-292,435,519) with a constant-time compare that equalizes the invalid-hex path (:587-609) and fails closed on a missing secret (:462-477).

src-tauri/src/engine/webhook.rs:521-529 wraps a body that fails JSON parsing as `{"raw": text}` and admits it, so the content-type allowlist stage is inverted into accept-anything; and :108 serves with no connection or read timeout, leaving a slow client to hold a connection indefinitely. The size cap is correct — a tower layer at :93 enforced during extraction, therefore ahead of both auth and parse.

src-tauri/src/engine/cloud_webhook_relay.rs mints events from a polled intermediary with no end-to-end verification at the final hop, which the technique forbids delegating to the middle, and its liveness is a literal `true` passed at every call site (:159,210,283,468) so a dead relay is indistinguishable from a live one.

src-tauri/src/commands/tools/triggers.rs:1742 replays the redaction placeholder rather than the delivery (set at webhook.rs:304), :1750-1761 re-signs from the stored secret so a replay always authenticates and can never reproduce a rejection verdict, and webhook.rs:273-284 logs every header verbatim with no filter — the signature, and any authorization or cookie a sender attached, all land in the record the body was redacted to protect.

src-tauri/src/engine/webhook.rs:629 mints a fresh UUID with no delivery-identity check and never reads `x-github-delivery`, so on the one mouth with mandatory authentication a sender's at-least-once retry fires the trigger a second time; smee_relay.rs:225-256 shows the correct bounded shape on a different mouth.

src-tauri/src/engine/background/lifecycle.rs:481 sets `webhook_alive` true before the port probe and before the bind, so `get_webhook_status` (triggers.rs:1250-1258) reports a listening ingress throughout the up-to-six-minute window in which nothing is bound, and :571-580 downgrades EADDRINUSE to a warn kept out of Sentry — the two-copies-own-the-port case the technique says must be loud. Graceful drain (webhook.rs:108-113) and the traffic-independent health route (:192-208) are conformant.

pairs.registryProposal: The technique pairs 'record everything, verbatim' with 'redact at write time' but never says what replay replays once redaction has run, and this repo fell straight into the gap: it redacted the whole body (webhook.rs:294-305) and thereby voided its own replay door (triggers.rs:1742) without anything failing. Proposal: state that redaction is field-scoped within the payload, never whole-body, precisely because a wholesale redaction silently converts the debugging lifeline into a placeholder generator; and where a system already keeps an encrypted verbatim copy elsewhere (as this one does at webhook.rs:634), the replay door must read from that copy and the record must name it. A second, smaller point: the technique says replay 're-earns admission', which this repo honours by re-POSTing through the live route — but it re-signs the payload to get past authentication, so the replay proves the pipeline works on a well-formed delivery and can never reproduce the rejection it was invoked to debug. Replay should carry the recorded signature, and a replay that now fails verification is a result, not a malfunction.
